textContent.text: Businessman John Paul DeJoria is known for becoming a self-made billionaire, but his road to success was not a smooth one. He would eventually co-found one of the most iconic brands of the 1980s and shift the way consumers think about beauty products and corporate responsibility. But first, he needed to find his way in business. DeJoria, who grew up in poverty, learned his earliest lessons about business success as a child. At the age of nine, in an effort to help support his family, he sold Christmas cards and newspapers. Poverty forced DeJoria and his brother into foster care for part of his childhood, but DeJoria remained optimistic and looked for ways to change his situation for the better.

In an effort to pay for college, DeJoria sold encyclopedias door-to-door. He later said that this job provided him valuable experience with rejection. It was during this time that he learned to stay positive and keep trying when people told him, "No." DeJoria carried these lessons of perseverance and zeal into his future business endeavors, helping him to eventually find success.

In 1980, DeJoria teamed up with his friend Paul Mitchell, a hair stylist who made his own hair care products. DeJoria saw how much customers valued Mitchell's products, so DeJoria suggested they build a company together. DeJoria, who had already spent several years working in management and sales for large hair care brands, felt confident that his skills, combined with Mitchell's products, could make a large impact on the industry. The two friends pooled their resources, and DeJoria borrowed some money from his mother. The result was $700—enough to buy supplies and start their business.

The friends' company, John Paul Mitchell Systems, sold Paul Mitchell products to professionals working at hair salons. DeJoria used his sales skills to go from salon to salon, convincing hair care experts to use Paul Mitchell products on their customers' hair. People quickly fell in love with the products, and after a few years, the company was making millions of dollars annually.

From the beginning, DeJoria and Mitchell wanted their company to reflect their values. They never tested their salon products on animals because they perceived animal testing as a cruel practice. John Paul Mitchell Systems was the first beauty care company to take a public stand against the practice of animal testing, paving the way for other brands to seek out more ethical alternatives. In addition, as John Paul Mitchell Systems grew, DeJoria and Mitchell made a commitment to use recycled materials in their product packaging. Not only did this have economic benefits, but this decision cemented the company's reputation as an industry leader in environmental awareness.

After many years of hard work leading John Paul Mitchell Systems and managing other companies he owned, DeJoria became very wealthy. Still grounded by the same commitment to progress and optimism that helped launch him into business, DeJoria became a notable philanthropist. He began giving money to environmental organizations and other causes that were close to his heart. In 2011, DeJoria signed "The Giving Pledge," promising to give away at least half his money to charitable causes. In the years since then, DeJoria has donated many millions of dollars, giving rise to his personal motto, "Success unshared is failure."

textContent.text: Farming's relationship with technology dates back to the Stone Age. Over ten thousand years ago, the earliest farmers designed stone tools that dramatically improved their ability to produce food. Since then, farmers have invented irrigation systems, horse-drawn plows, mechanical reapers, and gas-powered tractors, all while feeding a growing and increasingly interconnected global population. Today's farmers continue to look for new and better ways to farm by utilizing high-tech tools that allow them to produce more food while using fewer resources. The practice of implementing these new technologies, referred to as "smart agriculture," is revolutionizing food production.

Some tools used in smart agriculture rely heavily on data from satellites. Satellites allow farmers to track weather systems and to see how the weather has impacted their crops. In the past, farmers relied on their own senses, historical patterns, and perhaps a farmer's almanac to determine when to plant seeds, water crops, or start the harvest. Today's farmers have an advantage over farmers of the past. They often have electronic weather monitoring stations in their fields. These small weather stations use sensors to collect and analyze data on temperature, rainfall, humidity, and wind. A large farm might have several weather stations that send data over the internet. Computer programs can combine this data with predictive weather modeling to make pinpointed decisions about when to irrigate, plant, and harvest.

GPS technology, which also relies on satellites, allows tractors and other machines to navigate through the fields, even without drivers. In addition to utilizing driverless technology, smart agriculture often involves other types of autonomous machines that use artificial intelligence (AI). These machines can be used to plant seeds, thin overcrowded crops, remove weeds, and even bring in the harvest all on their own. They do so in part by using specialized optical sensors. These sensors allow the robotic machines to "see" what they are doing in the fields. Optical sensors may also be used on insect traps to identify agricultural pests that need to be controlled. AI enables drones to recognize unwanted weeds and spray them with chemicals without harming the surrounding crops. Drones can also take photos or videos that enable farmers to view faraway crops from a desktop monitor.

Farmers receive a lot of data from these specialized machines, so they use computer programs to help them analyze the information and make the best decisions for their crops and livestock. The data they receive ranges from soil temperature to moisture levels to animal health. The devices that the farmers use are connected to each other and to the internet. The devices communicate information that allows farmers to get a complex and constantly updated "big picture" of what is happening in the fields.

pieces.text: Smart agriculture is sometimes called

because, by utilizing these high-tech tools, farmers are able to use exactly the right resources in exactly the right places. This helps farmers save money, and it also helps them protect the environment. When farmers know just how much water their crops need, and exactly where it is needed, they waste less water. When they run their machines only when they are needed, they use less fuel, which reduces both expenses and air pollution. When farmers know just the right amount of fertilizer and pesticides they need to keep their crops healthy, they usually use much less. This helps keep the surrounding land, water, and wildlife healthier. Modern technology used in precision agriculture helps farmers produce more food for a growing population in ways that are potentially more sustainable and more profitable.

textContent.text: In 2021, JBS Foods, one of the world's largest meatpacking companies, was forced to suspend operations at many of its plants. The cause was a cyberattack; computer hackers broke into the company's computer system and froze all its data. The company was forced to pay the hackers eleven million dollars to regain access and resume business.

pieces.text: Attacks on computer systems are becoming more common in today's internet-connected world. While the internet improves our lives in many ways, it also leaves us vulnerable to new dangers. For instance, hackers can inject malware—such as computer viruses and other harmful computer code—into targeted networks. Malware can destroy a computer system or interfere with how it functions. As with JBS Foods, hackers can use malware called
to seize an entire computer system and all its data. The hackers then demand money as ransom to unfreeze it.

textContent.text: Cyberattacks affect not only large businesses but also individuals. Cybercriminals can hack into a computer network to steal valuable data, such as personal identification information, credit card numbers, and bank account numbers. Hackers may sell this information to other criminals or use it to break into and steal money from a person's accounts. This information can also be used for identity theft, a crime that occurs when a person pretends to be someone else in order to buy things or get bank loans. Identity theft affects millions of people every year. Victims often spend years trying to get their identities back and restore their credit.

How can people and businesses protect themselves from cyberattacks? That's where cybersecurity comes in. Cybersecurity is the practice of keeping online devices, data, and networks safe from attacks. Cybersecurity experts help track down and stop hackers. They develop computer software for guarding computers and sensitive information. These experts also share recommendations to help people stay safe while using the internet.

One important strategy for staying safe on the internet is choosing strong computer passwords. Cybersecurity experts advise specific protocols for generating secure passwords: they should be long, complex, and difficult to guess. Experts caution against using personal information, such as birthdays, pet names, or nicknames that could be found online. Experts also recommend using a different password for each account. Special password management programs can create strong passwords and safely store them so that you do not have to remember them all.

Another cybersecurity strategy is to be cautious when downloading anything from the internet to your computer or phone. Be wary of emails and texts from unknown senders. Opening an email, clicking on a link, or downloading an attachment could introduce malware into your system. Any email asking you to send personal information could be a scam. Fortunately, cybersecurity experts have created products to help keep our computers and data safe from viruses and other online hazards. For example, a firewall is software that can be installed on a computer system to monitor incoming emails and messages and block those that are suspicious. Similarly, antivirus software can scan a computer's system to find and flag dangerous malware so that it can be removed.

The programmers who develop these cybersecurity programs must constantly update their products. That's because hackers are always devising new ways to break into computer systems. Experts advise regularly updating your operating systems and any cybersecurity programs that you use. Thanks to cybersecurity strategies and experts who are always on the alert, we can all enjoy the benefits of the internet much more safely.

Cybersecurity experts help track down and stop hackers. They develop computer software for guarding computers and sensitive information. These experts also share recommendations to help people stay safe while using the internet.

One important strategy for staying safe on the internet is choosing strong computer passwords. Cybersecurity experts advise specific protocols for generating secure passwords: they should be long, complex, and difficult to guess. Experts caution against using personal information, such as birthdays, pet names, or nicknames that could be found online. Experts also recommend using a different password for each account. Special password management programs can create strong passwords and safely store them so that you do not have to remember them all.

Another cybersecurity strategy is to be cautious when downloading anything from the internet to your computer or phone. Be wary of emails and texts from unknown senders. Opening an email, clicking on a link, or downloading an attachment could introduce malware into your system. Any email asking you to send personal information could be a scam. Fortunately, cybersecurity experts have created products to help keep our computers and data safe from viruses and other online hazards. For example, a firewall is software that can be installed on a computer system to monitor incoming emails and messages and block those that are suspicious. Similarly, antivirus software can scan a computer's system to find and flag dangerous malware so that it can be removed.

The programmers who develop these cybersecurity programs must constantly update their products. That's because hackers are always devising new ways to break into computer systems. Experts advise regularly updating your operating systems and any cybersecurity programs that you use. Thanks to cybersecurity strategies and experts who are always on the alert, we can all enjoy the benefits of the internet much more safely.

textContent.text: Why would you pay for something you hope to never use? That's what people do when they purchase an insurance policy. Insurance helps minimize financial risk. Natural disasters, car crashes, and health crises are all types of mishaps that can happen suddenly and unexpectedly, and they can be expensive to recover from. This is when insurance—if purchased in advance—can help soften the blow.

Insurance companies like to say that they sell "peace of mind." The business is based on the idea of shared risk; the basic premise is that the financial risk is shared among the group instead of solely on the individual. Insurance companies take a "premium," or an amount of money in advance, from their customers and collect it to build a larger sum. Then when something happens to one of the customers, the insurance company gives the customer some of the collected money. The insurance company makes a profit by collecting more money than it pays out.

This business model has been around in some form or other for hundreds of years. One of the first insurance companies in North America, the Philadelphia Contributionship, was co-founded by Benjamin Franklin in 1752. At that time house fires were a common occurrence and often spread rapidly, which is what prompted Franklin to start the insurance company. Wooden homes were crowded together in the city of Philadelphia, and people used fire for cooking and heating. Homeowners who paid Franklin's company for fire insurance would receive a payment of money to rebuild their homes in the event of a fire. The funds for such payments came from the combined money that all the insurance holders paid to Franklin's company.

Over time, many other types of insurance have developed to protect customers against other risks. The most common types of insurance today include car insurance, homeowner's insurance, and health insurance. When purchasing insurance, customers are often asked to choose between different plans. Each plan has different premiums and different coverage. In the context of insurance, "coverage" means the insurance company agrees to cover at least some of the costs that arise in specified situations.

In the example of car insurance, car owners buy insurance so that they will not have to pay for all the damage that might result from a car accident. Most states require that drivers buy car insurance to cover the costs of damage they might cause to other people and their property. The insurance company sets the price for a car insurance policy based on the type of car, the driver's driving record, and other factors. If drivers never have any accidents or issues on the road, they will never receive any money from the insurance company. However, if they accidentally back into another car in a parking lot, or if their car gets crushed by a falling tree—and if those events are covered by the insurance policy—the company must pay to have the damage repaired.

Insurance companies can cover much more than homes and cars. For example, pet owners can purchase insurance to cover veterinary expenses if their pets become ill or injured. Travelers can buy trip insurance to cover costs in case of lost luggage, canceled flights, or medical problems while traveling. People can buy insurance for almost anything, if they are willing to pay the price. One famous soccer player even paid to insure his legs for millions of dollars! The insurance industry has certainly evolved in ways that Benjamin Franklin likely never imagined.

Natural disasters, car crashes, and health crises are all types of mishaps that can happen suddenly and unexpectedly, and they can be expensive to recover from. This is when insurance—if purchased in advance—can help soften the blow.

Insurance companies like to say that they sell "peace of mind." The business is based on the idea of shared risk; the basic premise is that the financial risk is shared among the group instead of solely on the individual. Insurance companies take a "premium," or an amount of money in advance, from their customers and collect it to build a larger sum. Then when something happens to one of the customers, the insurance company gives the customer some of the collected money. The insurance company makes a profit by collecting more money than it pays out.

This business model has been around in some form or other for hundreds of years. One of the first insurance companies in North America, the Philadelphia Contributionship, was co-founded by Benjamin Franklin in 1752. At that time house fires were a common occurrence and often spread rapidly, which is what prompted Franklin to start the insurance company. Wooden homes were crowded together in the city of Philadelphia, and people used fire for cooking and heating. Homeowners who paid Franklin's company for fire insurance would receive a payment of money to rebuild their homes in the event of a fire. The funds for such payments came from the combined money that all the insurance holders paid to Franklin's company.

Over time, many other types of insurance have developed to protect customers against other risks. The most common types of insurance today include car insurance, homeowner's insurance, and health insurance. When purchasing insurance, customers are often asked to choose between different plans. Each plan has different premiums and different coverage. In the context of insurance, "coverage" means the insurance company agrees to cover at least some of the costs that arise in specified situations.

In the example of car insurance, car owners buy insurance so that they will not have to pay for all the damage that might result from a car accident. Most states require that drivers buy car insurance to cover the costs of damage they might cause to other people and their property. The insurance company sets the price for a car insurance policy based on the type of car, the driver's driving record, and other factors. If drivers never have any accidents or issues on the road, they will never receive any money from the insurance company. However, if they accidentally back into another car in a parking lot, or if their car gets crushed by a falling tree—and if those events are covered by the insurance policy—the company must pay to have the damage repaired.

Insurance companies can cover much more than homes and cars. For example, pet owners can purchase insurance to cover veterinary expenses if their pets become ill or injured. Travelers can buy trip insurance to cover costs in case of lost luggage, canceled flights, or medical problems while traveling. People can buy insurance for almost anything, if they are willing to pay the price. One famous soccer player even paid to insure his legs for millions of dollars! The insurance industry has certainly evolved in ways that Benjamin Franklin likely never imagined.

textContent.text: Animal power was first harnessed for transportation around 8000 BCE. Early transportation technologies, such as the saddle and the wheel, enabled the development of trade routes and empires. In the twentieth century, combustion engine vehicles—cars and trucks powered by gasoline—became the main mode of personal transit. New technologies are changing the way people travel yet again as electric vehicles start to replace conventional cars. Today's automotive manufacturers are lining up behind two different kinds of electric vehicles in the competition for the future of the business.

The most common electric vehicles are battery electric vehicles (BEVs). A BEV runs on energy stored in a lithium-based battery, much like cell phones and laptops. The popularity of BEVs is growing, driven in part by government policies and fluctuating fuel prices, so more and more charging stations are appearing in public spaces.

BEVs have many convenient features, but there are still some bumps in the road when it comes to development. Because of the elements needed to make a lithium-based battery, production is expensive. Also, recharging this type of battery can take significantly longer than it takes to fill a gas tank. For many people, the time and effort that is needed to charge a BEV seems inconvenient and deters them from purchasing this type of car.

There is another kind of electric vehicle that can be refueled in minutes: a fuel cell electric vehicle (FCEV). FCEVs use hydrogen as fuel. Hydrogen is pumped into an FCEV's tank, much like gasoline is pumped into a gas-powered vehicle. In an FCEV's fuel cell, hydrogen is combined with oxygen from the surrounding air. A chemical reaction between the two causes a flow of electrons, and the electric current powers the vehicle. The only byproducts of the process are heat and water vapor, which is emitted from the car's tailpipe.

Since FCEVs are able to be refueled faster than BEVs, why do car manufacturers and consumers seem to prefer BEVs? One important factor is that hydrogen fueling stations are scarce and more expensive to build than BEV charging stations. Another problem with FCEVs is that hydrogen does not exist in its pure form in nature. The most common way to produce hydrogen is to extract it from natural gas, a process that releases carbon dioxide into the atmosphere. FCEVs also waste, or lose, more energy than BEVs. Energy is lost when hydrogen is produced and then when it is compressed into tanks. Still more energy is lost in the process of converting hydrogen into electricity. Altogether, about sixty percent of the energy used to power an FCEV is wasted, whereas only about twenty percent is lost in powering BEVs.

Because of these factors, BEVs far outnumber FCEVs on the road, but several automotive manufacturers continue to invest in developing FCEVs and hydrogen fueling networks. Both of these models have promising features, but no one knows exactly what will fuel the vehicles of tomorrow.

content.text: What is the text mainly about?

choices.text: It is about the reasons why FCEVs are the type of electrical vehicle most likely to replace gas-powered vehicles.
It is about how car manufacturers are working to make production of BEVs and FCEVs more efficient.
It is about the comparative advantages and disadvantages of two types of electric vehicles, BEVs and FCEVs.
It is about how natural gases like hydrogen and oxygen will be the transportation fuels of the future.

textContent.text: Animal power was first harnessed for transportation around 8000 BCE. Early transportation technologies, such as the saddle and the wheel, enabled the development of trade routes and empires. In the twentieth century, combustion engine vehicles—cars and trucks powered by gasoline—became the main mode of personal transit. New technologies are changing the way people travel yet again as electric vehicles start to replace conventional cars. Today's automotive manufacturers are lining up behind two different kinds of electric vehicles in the competition for the future of the business.

The most common electric vehicles are battery electric vehicles (BEVs). A BEV runs on energy stored in a lithium-based battery, much like cell phones and laptops. The popularity of BEVs is growing, driven in part by government policies and fluctuating fuel prices, so more and more charging stations are appearing in public spaces.

BEVs have many convenient features, but there are still some bumps in the road when it comes to development. Because of the elements needed to make a lithium-based battery, production is expensive. Also, recharging this type of battery can take significantly longer than it takes to fill a gas tank. For many people, the time and effort that is needed to charge a BEV seems inconvenient and deters them from purchasing this type of car.

There is another kind of electric vehicle that can be refueled in minutes: a fuel cell electric vehicle (FCEV). FCEVs use hydrogen as fuel. Hydrogen is pumped into an FCEV's tank, much like gasoline is pumped into a gas-powered vehicle. In an FCEV's fuel cell, hydrogen is combined with oxygen from the surrounding air. A chemical reaction between the two causes a flow of electrons, and the electric current powers the vehicle. The only byproducts of the process are heat and water vapor, which is emitted from the car's tailpipe.

Since FCEVs are able to be refueled faster than BEVs, why do car manufacturers and consumers seem to prefer BEVs? One important factor is that hydrogen fueling stations are scarce and more expensive to build than BEV charging stations. Another problem with FCEVs is that hydrogen does not exist in its pure form in nature. The most common way to produce hydrogen is to extract it from natural gas, a process that releases carbon dioxide into the atmosphere. FCEVs also waste, or lose, more energy than BEVs. Energy is lost when hydrogen is produced and then when it is compressed into tanks. Still more energy is lost in the process of converting hydrogen into electricity. Altogether, about sixty percent of the energy used to power an FCEV is wasted, whereas only about twenty percent is lost in powering BEVs.

Because of these factors, BEVs far outnumber FCEVs on the road, but several automotive manufacturers continue to invest in developing FCEVs and hydrogen fueling networks. Both of these models have promising features, but no one knows exactly what will fuel the vehicles of tomorrow.
